Sanjay — thanks for the clear recap and the diagram, that helps a lot. High-level answers below and proposed next steps. I'll loop Rishi for the deep technical suggestions.

1) SDK & auth
- Server-side API keys are fine for the POC. For per-user access later we recommend short-lived tokens (OAuth2) or a user-scoped token exchange on your backend.
- Key rotation: rotate keys every 90 days; maintain a key per-environment and deploy a key-id header (X-API-Key-Id) so you can revoke without churn.
- SDK: our official SDK supports automatic key refresh hooks and exposes an AuthProvider interface for integrating your KMS. See: https://docs.redwood.inference/sdk#auth-and-retries

2) Routing
- You can route by request intent header (e.g., X-Redwood-Intent: chat|batch|embed). Our router can map intents to pools: low-latency hosted pool vs high-throughput dedicated pool.
- Policy options: latency_min_sla, burst_capacity, and fallback_model. For chat mark requests as latency-critical; SDK has a .routeHint() you can set.

3) Structured output & tool calling
- Recommend schema-validated JSON output (we validate schemas server-side) and a tool-calling handshake: model returns a tool_call token + payload; backend verifies payload before executing actions.
- Use signed action tokens for critical actions (ticket create) and log execution IDs.

4) Rate limiting, retries & idempotency (short primer)
- Quotas: default hosted quotas are per-API-key and per-project. Specific POC numbers we can provision — typical starting quotas are 600 requests/minute and 50 concurrent tokens for chat; embeddings have separate throughput. For Dedicated we will size by reserved GPUs.
- 429 handling: always respect Retry-After header when present. If Retry-After is absent, use exponential backoff with full jitter (start 250ms, cap ~10s).
- Idempotency: include a unique idempotency key (X-Request-ID or Idempotency-Key) for any non-idempotent operation (e.g., generating billing-impacting outputs or tool actions). Server will store keys for a configurable window (we support 1-24 hours).
- Retries: client-side SDK will default to N=3 retries for idempotent calls with backoff; non-idempotent calls should not be auto-retried unless you supply an idempotency key.
- Status headers: we return remaining_quota and quota_reset_in in responses to help client backoff.

Next steps:
- I will share a short technical note with recommended SDK calls and header examples (auth, X-Redwood-Intent, Idempotency-Key).
- Marissa will follow up on commercial terms & provisioning Dedicated for your expected throughput.

Adding a couple of engineering details that Acme's infra team may find useful: 

- 429 best practice: prefer per-customer token-bucket server-side with a global smoothing window to avoid thundering herds. Push quota headers so clients can proactively throttle.
- Backoff: full jitter (Rand(0, base * 2^attempt)). Example: base=250ms, attempts=0.. => max backoff cap 10s. This avoids synchronized retries.
- Request IDs: use UUIDv4 in X-Request-ID and also include a short checksum in metadata (e.g., sha1(payload)[:8]) for dedupe on large payloads.
- Embeddings + Rerank: compute sparse+dense hybrid. Store embedding vectors with a document_id and a model_version tag; when reranking, include candidate_limit header and use a two-stage: approximate (FAISS) then rerank with model. Cache reranks for identical query signatures for 10-60s depending on freshness requirements.
- SDK hooks: instrument the SDK to surface quota warnings (<=20% remaining) and provide an onQuotaWarning callback so your app can degrade gracefully (e.g., fall back to cached answer or condensed responses).

Happy to share a sample middleware we use for idempotency and backoff if helpful.
